summary: Skyrise revolves around a spatial blind-bidding system where you place numbered tiles on a grid and adjacency/value determines who wins which building site, so every round is a tense read of what everyone else wants. Beyond the auction, it's a fairly standard tile-laying/set-collection engine about building neighborhoods, courting patrons, and chasing objectives, but the bidding is what people remember.
praised: The unique spatial auction/bidding mechanism is genuinely novel and tense
High player interaction — reading opponents and predicting their bids matters a lot
Attractive, colorful production and satisfying city-building visuals
Multiple viable scoring paths keep replayability high
criticised: The bidding system has a steep learning curve and is hard to teach cleanly
Analysis paralysis can creep in as players overthink bids
Some randomness from patron/objective card draws feels swingy to some players
Can run long, especially at 4 players, given the deliberation the auction invites

interaction.kind: blind spatial bidding and area denial

scoring.why: Points come from neighborhood majorities, patron cards, secret/public objectives, and the Wonder, so winning requires balancing several scoring engines rather than maxing one.
